newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt loses vote on disputed labour pact.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt loses vote on disputed labour pact.

text.p: The Italian government's controversial labour bill was defeated by a parliamentary commission on Wednesday after the ruling coalition's hard-left ally abstained in the vote.

However, political sources said the defeat did not represent a serious setback for the bill, which aims to simplify procedures to free up public expenditure on jobs and boost flexibility in the labour market.
The Communist Refoundation abstained in the lower house of parliament's productive activity committee, ensuring that the centre-left majority lost the motion.
Refoundation has protested at measures contained in the bill which are designed to encourage part-time employment.
The package is due to be voted on in the full lower house on May 14.
The draft bill was approved by the Italian cabinet last month and is designed to complete provisions made in a September pact between government, unions and employers to boost jobs.

However the package has already been watered down in the various parliamentary commissions and industrialists' federation Confindustria, which signed the original accord last year, has demanded that the changes be reversed.
Confindustria chairman Giorgio Fossa warned that unless the package returned to its original form he would disassociate himself from it. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
